    AI Overview
    Ozempic (semaglutide) is an FDA-approved, once-weekly injection that improves blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes and reduces the risk of cardiovascular events like heart attacks or strokes. By mimicking the GLP-1 hormone, it increases insulin release and reduces appetite, often leading to weight loss as a side effect. 
    Key Details 
    • Uses: Primarily for type 2 diabetes management, with added cardiovascular benefits for high-risk individuals.
    • How it Works: It mimics a natural hormone, GLP-1, which regulates appetite and slows gastric emptying, making you feel full longer.
    • Side Effects: Common side effects are primarily gastrointestinal, including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and constipation.
    • FDA Status: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes, but not for weight loss, although it is often used off-label for that purpose (the same ingredient is approved for weight loss under the name Wegovy).
    • Interactions/Warnings: It may increase the risk of thyroid tumors. It should not be used by individuals with a family history of Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma (MTC) or MEN 2 syndrome. 
    Ozempic is manufactured by Novo Nordisk and is typically administered as a weekly, self-administered subcutaneous injection.

    What happens in the body when you take Ozempic?
    Ozempic increases the levels of incretins – hormones – which are naturally produced by the stomach when you eat. It works by helping your body to produce more insulin when needed. It also reduces the amount of glucose, or sugar, produced by the liver, and slows down how quickly food is digested.

    AI Overview
    Semaglutide (sold as Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus) acts as a GLP-1 receptor agonist, mimicking the GLP-1 hormone to regulate appetite, slow digestion, and manage blood sugar. It reduces hunger by targeting brain receptors, increases satiety by slowing gastric emptying, and stimulates insulin release while reducing glucagon, aiding in weight loss and diabetes management. 
    How Semaglutide Works:
    • Appetite Regulation (Brain):
      Semaglutide mimics the GLP-1 hormone, which travels to the hypothalamus in the brain, signaling that the body is full, reducing hunger and cravings. 
    • Slowing Gastric Emptying (Gut):
      The medication slows the rate at which the stomach empties, ensuring food stays in the stomach longer, promoting prolonged fullness and lower calorie intake. 
    • Insulin Regulation (Pancreas):
      It stimulates the pancreas to release insulin when blood sugar levels are high after meals and suppresses the release of glucagon, which helps manage blood glucose levels. 
    Key Effects of Semaglutide:
    • Weight Loss: By reducing hunger and slowing digestion, patients consume fewer calories, leading to significant weight loss (approx. 15% in studies). 
    • Blood Sugar Control: It improves glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes. 
    • Cardiovascular Benefits: Studies indicate it can reduce risks of heart attack, stroke, or cardiovascular death in patients with obesity or cardiovascular disease. 
    Common Side Effects:
    Due to its action on the digestive system, common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, and abdominal pain.

      AI Overview
      Semaglutide is available under three main brand names developed by Novo Nordisk, each approved for specific uses: Ozempic (type 2 diabetes), Wegovy (weight management), and Rybelsus (oral tablets for type 2 diabetes). These medications are glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, which improve blood sugar and promote weight loss. 
      • Wegovy (Injection):
        Approved for long-term weight management in individuals with obesity or overweight with related health conditions. 
      • Ozempic (Injection):
        Approved for managing type 2 diabetes and reducing the risk of cardiovascular events (heart attack, stroke) in adults with both type 2 diabetes and heart disease. 
      • Rybelsus (Tablet):
        The only FDA-approved oral (pill) formulation of semaglutide used to improve blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes. 
      These medications are not identical in dosage or formulation, although they share the same active ingredient. They must be prescribed by a healthcare provider.

        Drug Interactions. What are the drug interactions of semaglutide?
        About this result
        Feedback
        An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
        AI Overview
        Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus) primarily interacts with diabetes medications (insulin, sulfonylureas) by increasing hypoglycemia risk and with oral drugs by slowing gastric emptying, which delays their absorption. Key interactions include thyroid medicines, blood thinners like warfarin, andCertain herbs. 
        Major Drug Interactions
        • Diabetes Medications (Insulin, Sulfonylureas):
          Combining semaglutide with insulin or sulfonylureas (e.g., glipizide, glimepiride) significantly increases the risk of hypoglycemia (low blood sugar). 
        • Oral Medications:
          Because semaglutide slows stomach emptying, it can reduce the speed and extent of absorption for many oral medications (e.g., warfarin, antibiotics like ciprofloxacin). 
        • Levothyroxine:
          Reduced absorption of oral levothyroxine can occur, requiring monitoring for thyroid dysfunction. 
        • Warfarin/Anticoagulants:
          While studies show variable results, close monitoring of INR (blood clotting tests) is recommended when starting semaglutide. 
        • Other GLP-1 Agents:
          Do not combine semaglutide with other GLP-1 receptor agonists (e.g., liraglutide, dulaglutide) as they are in the same class. 
        Important Considerations
        • Oral Medications (Rybelsus):
          Should be taken on an empty stomach with a small amount of water, with no other food or beverages for 30 minutes to ensure absorption. 
        • Supplements/Herbs:
          Gymnema, prickly pear, bitter melon, and fenugreek might increase the risk of low blood sugar. 
        Disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only. Always consult your doctor or pharmacist regarding drug interactions.

          AI Overview
          As of April 2026, semaglutide is FDA-approved for Type 2 diabetes (Ozempic/Rybelsus), weight management (Wegovy), cardiovascular risk reduction, and chronic kidney disease management. A high-dose, once-daily oral Wegovy pill was approved in late 2025 for chronic weight management and cardiovascular risk. 
          FDA Approval Status & Usage Examples (2026)
          • Wegovy (Injectable & Oral): Approved for chronic weight management in adults and children (12+) with obesity, and adults with overweight plus at least one weight-related condition (e.g., hypertension, type 2 diabetes). It is also approved to reduce risks of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). 
          • Ozempic (Injectable): Approved for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes, reduction of cardiovascular risk (stroke, heart attack) in adults with diabetes, and for treating chronic kidney disease. 
          • Rybelsus (Oral Pill): Approved for glycemic control in type 2 diabetes. 
          Synonyms and Brand Names
          Semaglutide is marketed under three primary brand names, each with specific, often overlapping, FDA approvals: 
          • Ozempic: (subcutaneous injection).
          • Wegovy: (subcutaneous injection & oral pill).
          • Rybelsus: (oral pill).
          Important Safety & Status Notes
          • Compounded Versions:
            The FDA has warned against the use of compounded (generic) semaglutide, noting that these versions are not FDA-approved, unlike the branded products from Novo Nordisk. 
          • Usage Examples:
            It is commonly used for managing glycemic levels, reducing weight by roughly
            15%15 %
            or more in studies, and reducing major cardiovascular complications.

            AI Overview
            Semaglutide is available in three primary brand-name forms manufactured by Novo Nordisk: Ozempic (injection for type 2 diabetes), Wegovy (injection for weight management), and Rybelsus (oral tablet for type 2 diabetes). Injections are administered weekly, while Rybelsus is a daily pill. 
            Key Forms of Semaglutide:
            • Wegovy (Injection): Approved for chronic weight management. Available in doses up to 2.4 mg. 
            • Ozempic (Injection): Approved for type 2 diabetes and reduction of cardiovascular risk. Doses include 0.25 mg, 0.5 mg, 1 mg, and 2 mg. 
            • Rybelsus (Tablet): The only oral GLP-1 receptor agonist, approved for type 2 diabetes. Available in 3 mg, 7 mg, and 14 mg doses. 
            Key Considerations:
            • Administration:
              Ozempic and Wegovy are once-weekly subcutaneous injections. Rybelsus is a once-daily tablet taken on an empty stomach. 
            • Compound Semaglutide:
              Some pharmacies may offer compounded versions, but these are not FDA-approved and may use a different "salt" form rather than the regulated base form. 
            All forms work by mimicking a hormone called GLP-1 to lower blood sugar and reduce appetite.
